390: // --- Frontier API key ------------------------------------------------------
391: 
392: // checkFrontierKeyFn validates the configured frontier API key by
393: // issuing a GET /v1/models with a Bearer header. A 200 means the
394: // key is accepted; 401/403 means the key is bad; any other status
395: // is reported as-is so the operator can investigate.
396: //
397: // When cfg.FrontierKey is empty we skip with a hint: the proxy still
398: // runs without a frontier key (local + fusion degrade), but any
399: // frontier-bound request will 401.
400: func checkFrontierKeyFn(ctx context.Context, cfg config.Config, opts Options) Check {
401: 	if !cfg.FrontierEnabled() {
402: 		return Check{
403: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
404: 			Status: StatusSkip,
405: 			Detail: "no NEXUS_FRONTIER_API_KEY set — frontier routing will return 401",
406: 		}
407: 	}
408: 	base, err := frontierBaseURL(cfg.FrontierURL)
409: 	if err != nil {
410: 		return Check{
411: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
412: 			Status: StatusFail,
413: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("invalid NEXUS_FRONTIER_URL %q: %v", cfg.FrontierURL, err),
414: 		}
415: 	}
416: 	target := strings.TrimRight(base, "/") + "/models"
417: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, opts.Timeout)
418: 	defer cancel()
419: 	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, target, nil)
420: 	if err != nil {
421: 		return Check{
422: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
423: 			Status: StatusFail,
424: 			Detail: err.Error(),
425: 		}
426: 	}
427: 	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+cfg.FrontierKey)
428: 	resp, err := opts.HTTPClient.Do(req)
429: 	if err != nil {
430: 		return Check{
431: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
432: 			Status: StatusFail,
433: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("cannot reach %s: %v", target, err),
434: 		}
435: 	}
436: 	defer resp.Body.Close()
437: 	switch {
438: 	case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK:
439: 		return Check{
440: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
441: 			Status: StatusPass,
442: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("key accepted (endpoint: %s)", cfg.FrontierURL),
443: 		}
444: 	case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusUnauthorized, resp.StatusCode == http.StatusForbidden:
445: 		return Check{
446: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
447: 			Status: StatusFail,
448: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("endpoint rejected the key (status %d)", resp.StatusCode),
449: 		}
450: 	default:
451: 		return Check{
452: 			Name:   checkFrontierKey,
453: 			Status: StatusFail,
454: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("unexpected status %d from %s", resp.StatusCode, target),
455: 		}
456: 	}
457: }

459: // frontierBaseURL strips the per-endpoint suffix (/chat/completions
460: // is the only supported shape today) from cfg.FrontierURL so we can
461: // hit /v1/models for the key-validation probe. Falls back to the raw
462: // URL when no recognised suffix is present — in that case we issue
463: // the probe against the configured URL itself and let the server
464: // reject it.
465: func frontierBaseURL(raw string) (string, error) {
466: 	if raw == "" {
467: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("empty url")
468: 	}
469: 	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
470: 	if err != nil {
471: 		return "", err
472: 	}
473: 	if !strings.HasSuffix(u.Path, "/chat/completions") {
474: 		return raw, nil
475: 	}
476: 	u.Path = strings.TrimSuffix(u.Path, "/chat/completions")
477: 	return u.String(), nil
478: }

503: // --- VRAM probe ------------------------------------------------------------
504: 
505: // checkVRAMProbeFn drives the Ollama probe directly (no Manager —
506: // the diagnostic command is one-shot and should not spin up a
507: // goroutine) and reports the resulting budget. A non-zero budget is
508: // pass; zero budget (no signal) is warn — the handler falls back to
509: // the static NEXUS_TOKEN_GUARDRAIL in that case, which still serves
510: // traffic but loses the dynamic-aware behaviour the PRD promises.
511: //
512: // When NVIDIA GPUs are detected (issue #775), per-GPU VRAM status is
513: // included in the detail line: "GPU 0: 8.2 GiB free, GPU 1: 8.2 GiB free".
514: func checkVRAMProbeFn(ctx context.Context, cfg config.Config, opts Options) Check {
515: 	p := probe.NewOllamaProbe(opts.OllamaURL, opts.HTTPClient)
516: 	p.BytesPerToken = cfg.ProbeBytesPerToken
517: 	if opts.SysfsRoot != "" {
518: 		p.SysfsRoot = opts.SysfsRoot
519: 	}
520: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, opts.Timeout)
521: 	defer cancel()
522: 	b, err := p.Budget(ctx)
523: 	if err != nil {
524: 		return Check{
525: 			Name:   checkVRAMProbe,
526: 			Status: StatusWarn,
527: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("probe produced no budget: %v (falling back to NEXUS_TOKEN_GUARDRAIL=%d)", err, cfg.TokenGuardrail),
528: 		}
529: 	}
530: 	if b.Disabled() {
531: 		return Check{
532: 			Name:   checkVRAMProbe,
533: 			Status: StatusWarn,
534: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("budget disabled (source=%s) — falling back to NEXUS_TOKEN_GUARDRAIL=%d", b.Source, cfg.TokenGuardrail),
535: 		}
536: 	}
537: 	detail := fmt.Sprintf("budget: %d tokens (source: %s)", b.Tokens, b.Source)
538: 	if gpus, gerr := probe.ReadPerGPUVRAM(); gerr == nil && len(gpus) > 0 {
539: 		var parts []string
540: 		for _, g := range gpus {
541: 			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("GPU %d: %.1f GiB free", g.Index, float64(g.MemoryFree)/(1024*1024*1024)))
542: 		}
543: 		if len(parts) > 0 {
544: 			detail += "; " + strings.Join(parts, ", ")
545: 		}
546: 	}
547: 	return Check{
548: 		Name:   checkVRAMProbe,
549: 		Status: StatusPass,
550: 		Detail: detail,
551: 	}
552: }

554: // --- RAG examples directory ------------------------------------------------
555: 
556: // checkRAGDirectoryFn inspects cfg.ExamplesDir. A missing directory
557: // is a warning (not a failure) because RAG silently no-ops on an
558: // empty store and the proxy still serves traffic; the operator
559: // simply will not get the few-shot boost.
560: func checkRAGDirectoryFn(cfg config.Config) Check {
561: 	if cfg.ExamplesDir == "" {
562: 		return Check{
563: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
564: 			Status: StatusWarn,
565: 			Detail: "no NEXUS_EXAMPLES_DIR configured",
566: 		}
567: 	}
568: 	info, err := os.Stat(cfg.ExamplesDir)
569: 	if err != nil {
570: 		return Check{
571: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
572: 			Status: StatusWarn,
573: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("cannot stat %q: %v", cfg.ExamplesDir, err),
574: 		}
575: 	}
576: 	if !info.IsDir() {
577: 		return Check{
578: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
579: 			Status: StatusWarn,
580: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%q is not a directory", cfg.ExamplesDir),
581: 		}
582: 	}
583: 	entries, err := os.ReadDir(cfg.ExamplesDir)
584: 	if err != nil {
585: 		return Check{
586: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
587: 			Status: StatusWarn,
588: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("cannot read %q: %v", cfg.ExamplesDir, err),
589: 		}
590: 	}
591: 	if len(entries) == 0 {
592: 		return Check{
593: 			Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
594: 			Status: StatusWarn,
595: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%q is empty — RAG injection inactive", cfg.ExamplesDir),
596: 		}
597: 	}
598: 	return Check{
599: 		Name:   checkRAGDirectory,
600: 		Status: StatusPass,
601: 		Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d file(s) in %q", len(entries), cfg.ExamplesDir),
602: 	}
603: }

605: // --- Writable on-disk paths ------------------------------------------------
606: 
607: // checkWritablePathFn tries to os.CreateTemp in the parent directory
608: // of path. An empty path (operator opted out) is reported as skip
609: // — there is nothing to check.
610: func checkWritablePathFn(checkName, path string) Check {
611: 	if path == "" {
612: 		return Check{
613: 			Name:   checkName,
614: 			Status: StatusSkip,
615: 			Detail: "path not configured",
616: 		}
617: 	}
618: 	parent := filepath.Dir(path)
619: 	// filepath.Dir of a bare filename (no slashes) returns "." —
620: 	// the temp-file probe will use the cwd, which is what we want.
621: 	f, err := os.CreateTemp(parent, "nexus-check-*")
622: 	if err != nil {
623: 		return Check{
624: 			Name:   checkName,
625: 			Status: StatusFail,
626: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("cannot write to %q: %v", path, err),
627: 		}
628: 	}
629: 	tmpName := f.Name()
630: 	_ = f.Close()
631: 	_ = os.Remove(tmpName)
632: 	return Check{
633: 		Name:   checkName,
634: 		Status: StatusPass,
635: 		Detail: fmt.Sprintf("writable (%s)", path),
636: 	}
637: }

639: // --- Judge readiness -------------------------------------------------------
640: 
641: // checkJudgeReadinessFn inspects the judge configuration. The judge
642: // is dormant when sample rate is zero or required fields are empty;

644: // A partially configured judge (URL set but API key missing) is

850: 		}
851: 	}

853: 	// Construct the Nexus URL from cfg.Addr. The addr format is
854: 	// ":8000" (colon-prefixed port) or "localhost:8000". We prepend
855: 	// "http://" unconditionally because TLS config is a separate
856: 	// concern not relevant for a local diagnostic probe.
857: 	addr := cfg.Addr
858: 	if addr == "" {

860: 	}
861: 	// addr like ":8000" -> host "localhost:8000"

864: 	}
865: 	nexusURL := "http://" + addr + "/v1/models"
866: 
867: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, opts.Timeout)
868: 	defer cancel()
869: 	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, nexusURL, nil)
870: 	if err != nil {
871: 		return Check{
872: 			Name:   checkModelsEndpoint,
873: 			Status: StatusFail,
874: 			Detail: err.Error(),
875: 		}
876: 	}
877: 
878: 	resp, err := opts.HTTPClient.Do(req)
879: 	if err != nil {

881: 		// so `nexus check` can validate config even when the server is down.
882: 		return Check{
883: 			Name:   checkModelsEndpoint,
884: 			Status: StatusSkip,
885: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("cannot reach %s (is the Nexus server running?)", nexusURL),
886: 		}
887: 	}
888: 	defer resp.Body.Close()
889: 
890: 	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
891: 		return Check{
892: 			Name:   checkModelsEndpoint,
893: 			Status: StatusFail,
894: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("/v1/models returned status %d", resp.StatusCode),
895: 		}
896: 	}
897: 
898: 	// Read and parse the response body.
899: 	body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20)) // 1 MiB cap
900: 	if err != nil {
901: 		return Check{
902: 			Name:   checkModelsEndpoint,
903: 			Status: StatusFail,
904: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("failed to read /v1/models response: %v", err),
905: 		}
906: 	}
907: 
908: 	var listResp struct {
909: 		Data []struct {
910: 			ID string `json:"id"`
911: 		} `json:"data"`
912: 	}
913: 	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &listResp); err != nil {
914: 		return Check{
915: 			Name:   checkModelsEndpoint,
916: 			Status: StatusFail,
917: 			Detail: fmt.Sprintf("/v1/models returned invalid JSON: %v", err),
918: 		}
919: 	}
920: 
921: 	// Build a set of model IDs from the response.
922: 	seen := make(map[string]bool)
923: 	for _, m := range listResp.Data {
924: 		seen[m.ID] = true
925: 	}

939: 		}
940: 	}

362: 		}
363: 		latencyHist = c.latencyFrontier
364: 		ttftHist = c.ttftFrontier
365: 	}
366: 	if e.RAGInjected {
367: 		c.ragHitsTotal.Add(1)
368: 	} else {
369: 		c.ragMissesTotal.Add(1)
370: 	}
371: 	if e.TOONCompressed {
372: 		c.toonCompressedTotal.Add(1)
373: 	}
374: 	if e.Degraded {
375: 		c.degradedTotal.Add(1)
376: 	}
377: 	if e.InputTokens > 0 {
378: 		c.inputTokensTotal.Add(uint64(e.InputTokens))
379: 	}
380: 	if e.OutputTokens > 0 {
381: 		c.outputTokensTotal.Add(uint64(e.OutputTokens))
382: 	}
383: 	if e.TOONSavingsTokens > 0 {
384: 		c.toonSavingsTokensTotal.Add(uint64(e.TOONSavingsTokens))
385: 	}
386: 	if e.EstimatedCostUSD > 0 {
387: 		atomicAddFloat(&c.estimatedCostUSDBits, e.EstimatedCostUSD)
388: 	}
389: 	if e.TotalLatencyMs > 0 && latencyHist != nil {
390: 		latencyHist.Observe(float64(e.TotalLatencyMs))
391: 	}
392: 	if e.TTFTMs > 0 && ttftHist != nil {
393: 		ttftHist.Observe(float64(e.TTFTMs))
394: 	}
395: 	// Per-stage pipeline latency histograms (issue #300).
396: 	if e.RAGRetrievalMs > 0 {
397: 		c.stageRAG.Observe(float64(e.RAGRetrievalMs))
398: 	}
399: 	if e.PromptEngineeringMs > 0 {
400: 		c.stagePromptEng.Observe(float64(e.PromptEngineeringMs))
401: 	}
402: 	if e.TOONCompressionMs > 0 {
403: 		c.stageTOON.Observe(float64(e.TOONCompressionMs))
404: 	}
405: 	if e.SLMRoutingMs > 0 {
406: 		c.stageSLM.Observe(float64(e.SLMRoutingMs))
407: 	}
408: 	if e.UpstreamFirstByteMs > 0 {
409: 		c.stageUpstream.Observe(float64(e.UpstreamFirstByteMs))
410: 	}
411: 	// SLM confidence histogram (issue #425). Recorded when both
412: 	// Confidence > 0 and TaskType is a known category. A zero
413: 	// confidence means the SLM was not consulted (guardrail/DSL
414: 	// path); an empty TaskType means cache hit or no confidence
415: 	// store was wired.
416: 	if e.SLMConfidence > 0 && e.SLMTaskType != "" {
417: 		c.ObserveSLMConfidence(e.SLMTaskType, e.SLMConfidence)
418: 	}
419: }

462: // ObserveLatency records a latency observation for percentile computation
463: // (issue #774). route is the routing decision ("local", "frontier", "fusion").
464: // latencyMs is the total request latency in milliseconds. Safe for concurrent use.
465: func (c *Collector) ObserveLatency(route string, latencyMs int64) {
466: 	if c == nil || latencyMs <= 0 {
467: 		return
468: 	}
469: 	c.latencyPercentilesMu.RLock()
470: 	buf, ok := c.latencyPercentiles[route]
471: 	c.latencyPercentilesMu.RUnlock()
472: 	if ok && buf != nil {
473: 		buf.Observe(float64(latencyMs))
474: 		return
475: 	}
476: 	// Lazily create buffer
477: 	c.latencyPercentilesMu.Lock()
478: 	if c.latencyPercentiles == nil {
479: 		c.latencyPercentiles = make(map[string]*latencyPercentileBuffer)
480: 	}
481: 	buf, ok = c.latencyPercentiles[route]
482: 	if !ok || buf == nil {
483: 		buf = newLatencyPercentileBuffer(defaultLatencyBufferCapacity)
484: 		c.latencyPercentiles[route] = buf
485: 	}
486: 	c.latencyPercentilesMu.Unlock()
487: 	buf.Observe(float64(latencyMs))
488: }

544: // authentications. The /metrics renderer exposes it under the gauge

554: // IncRateLimit bumps the appropriate rate-limit counter for scope
555: // (one of "global", "per_client"). The middleware packages own the
556: // mapping from configuration to scope label.
557: //
558: // A scope other than "global" or "per_client" is silently ignored
559: // rather than treated as a default — the renderer only knows those
560: // two label values, so a third bucket would be invisible. Invalid
561: // scopes indicate a wiring bug worth surfacing in logs at the call
562: // site rather than silently dropping.
563: func (c *Collector) IncRateLimit(scope string, allowed bool) {
564: 	switch scope {
565: 	case "global":
566: 		if allowed {
567: 			c.rateLimitAllowedGlobal.Add(1)
568: 		} else {
569: 			c.rateLimitRejectedGlobal.Add(1)
570: 		}
571: 	case "per_client":
572: 		if allowed {
573: 			c.rateLimitAllowedPerClient.Add(1)
574: 		} else {
575: 			c.rateLimitRejectedPerClient.Add(1)
576: 		}
577: 	}
578: }

617: // --- Circuit breaker instrumentation (issue #304) --------------------
618: //
619: // RecordCircuitFailure records a failure for the named circuit and
620: // transitions its state to "open". Called from the chat handler when

653: // CircuitBreakerGauges returns the live state of all tracked circuit
654: // breakers as gauge samples for the Prometheus renderer. Each circuit
655: // emits three samples: state (0=closed, 1=half_open, 2=open),
656: // failures_total, and last_failure_seconds.
657: func (c *Collector) CircuitBreakerGauges() []GaugeSample {
658: 	var out []GaugeSample
659: 	c.cbMu.RLock()
660: 	defer c.cbMu.RUnlock()
661: 	for name, cb := range c.cbState {
662: 		lastFail := cb.lastFailure.Load()
663: 		labels := map[string]string{"circuit": name}
664: 		out = append(out,
665: 			GaugeSample{Name: "nexus_circuit_breaker_state", Labels: labels, Value: float64(cb.state.Load())},
666: 			GaugeSample{Name: "nexus_circuit_breaker_failures_total", Labels: labels, Value: float64(cb.failures.Load())},
667: 			GaugeSample{Name: "nexus_circuit_breaker_last_failure_seconds", Labels: labels, Value: float64(lastFail)},
668: 		)
669: 	}
670: 	return out
671: }

811: // --- RAG similarity histogram (issue #447) ------------------------------
812: //
813: // ObserveRAGSimilarity records one similarity observation for the
814: // given (path, outcome, threshold) tuple (issue #447, #671).
815: // Called from the RAG observer closure in main.go when
816: // handlers.RAGEvent carries a non-empty IndexPath.
817: //
818: // The outcome is "hit" when the retrieval returned a snippet above the
819: // configured threshold and "miss" otherwise; both observations land in
820: // the same bucket layout so the bucket counts can be directly compared.
821: // Score values outside [0, 1] are clamped to the [0, 1] range so a
822: // buggy embedder cannot push an observation into the +Inf bucket
823: // spuriously — the cosine contract is that similarity is bounded by 1.
824: //
825: // path values outside the fixed set ("hnsw", "brute_force") are
826: // silently dropped rather than bucketed under a third label, to
827: // preserve the bounded-cardinality contract documented for
828: // nexus_rag_similarity_histogram.
829: //
830: // effectiveThreshold is the similarity floor that was applied for this
831: // retrieval (issue #671). When per-directory overrides are configured,
832: // this may differ from the global NEXUS_RAG_THRESHOLD. Operators use
833: // the threshold label to tune per-domain thresholds.
834: func (c *Collector) ObserveRAGSimilarity(path, outcome string, score, effectiveThreshold float64) {
835: 	if score < 0 {
836: 		score = 0
837: 	} else if score > 1 {
838: 		score = 1
839: 	}
840: 	key := ragSimilarityKey(path, outcome, effectiveThreshold)
841: 	c.ragSimilarityMu.RLock()
842: 	h, ok := c.ragSimilarityHistograms[key]
843: 	c.ragSimilarityMu.RUnlock()
844: 	if !ok || h == nil {
845: 		// Lazily create histogram for this (path, outcome, threshold) combination
846: 		// (issue #671). This allows per-directory threshold tuning visibility
847: 		// without pre-allocating histograms for every possible threshold.
848: 		c.ragSimilarityMu.Lock()
849: 		// Double-check after acquiring write lock
850: 		if h, ok = c.ragSimilarityHistograms[key]; !ok || h == nil {
851: 			h = NewHistogram(RAGSimilarityBuckets)
852: 			c.ragSimilarityHistograms[key] = h
853: 		}
854: 		c.ragSimilarityMu.Unlock()
855: 	}
856: 	h.Observe(score)
857: }
858: 
859: // RAGSimilarityHistograms returns the per-(path, outcome, threshold) RAG
860: // similarity histograms for rendering. The map is keyed by
861: // "path|outcome|threshold" (e.g. "hnsw|hit|0.55"); callers iterate the keys to
862: // emit nexus_rag_similarity_histogram_bucket lines (issue #671).
863: //
864: // Returns nil when the collector is not yet initialised (e.g. when a
865: // nil receiver is passed to RenderPrometheus). Safe to call from
866: // multiple goroutines — returns a snapshot reference to the internal
867: // map, which is never mutated after NewCollector returns.
868: func (c *Collector) RAGSimilarityHistograms() map[string]*Histogram {
869: 	c.ragSimilarityMu.RLock()
870: 	defer c.ragSimilarityMu.RUnlock()
871: 	return c.ragSimilarityHistograms
872: }

874: // --- Rate-limit bucket utilization histogram (issue #746) ---------------
875: //
876: // ObserveRateLimitUtilization records one utilization observation for the
877: // given bucket ID. The utilization value is clamped to [0, 1] so a
878: // buggy caller cannot push an observation past the +Inf bucket
879: // spuriously. Histograms are created lazily per bucket ID.
880: func (c *Collector) ObserveRateLimitUtilization(bucketID string, utilizationPct float64) {
881: 	if bucketID == "" || c == nil {
882: 		return
883: 	}
884: 	if utilizationPct < 0 {

199: // LoadYAML reads configuration from a YAML file at path, then overlays
200: // environment variables so env always wins. This lets operators manage
201: // a config.yaml in K8s ConfigMaps while still overriding individual values
202: // via Secrets or env vars in the pod spec.
203: //
204: // The YAML file may omit any field; missing values fall back to the
205: // same defaults as Load. An error is returned when the file cannot be
206: // read or contains malformed YAML.
207: func LoadYAML(path string) (Config, error) {
208: 	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Clean(path))
209: 	if err != nil {
210: 		return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("config: cannot read config.yaml %q: %w", path, err)
211: 	}
212: 
213: 	// Pre-pass: inspect raw YAML values for boolean fields that must be
214: 	// valid bools. This catches "toon_unfenced: maybe" before yaml.Unmarshal
215: 	// silently leaves the field at its zero value (false), which would then
216: 	// be incorrectly interpreted as the default.
217: 	if err := validateRawBoolFields(data); err != nil {
218: 		return Config{}, err
219: 	}
220: 
221: 	var yc YAMLConfig
222: 	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &yc); err != nil {
223: 		return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("config: cannot unmarshal config.yaml %q: %w", path, err)
224: 	}
225: 
226: 	// Validate YAML-sourced fields that have constraints. These are
227: 	// checked here so the error is returned before any env override runs.
228: 	if err := yc.validate(); err != nil {
229: 		return Config{}, err
230: 	}
231: 
232: 	// Seed from YAML values (these are the "soft defaults").
233: 	cfg, err := yc.toConfig()
234: 	if err != nil {
235: 		return Config{}, err
236: 	}
237: 
238: 	// Now apply env overrides on top of the YAML seed.
239: 	// The logic mirrors Load() but reads from os.Getenv directly
240: 	// so that an explicitly set env var overrides the YAML value.
241: 
242: 	// Server
243: 	if v := os.Getenv("NEXUS_ADDR"); v != "" {
244: 		cfg.Addr = v
245: 	}
246: 	if v := os.Getenv("NEXUS_SERVER_READ_TIMEOUT"); v != "" {
247: 		d, err := time.ParseDuration(v)
248: 		if err != nil {
249: 			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("config: NEXUS_SERVER_READ_TIMEOUT: %w", err)
250: 		}
251: 		if d < 0 {
252: 			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("config: NEXUS_SERVER_READ_TIMEOUT must not be negative, got %s", d)
253: 		}
254: 		cfg.ReadTimeout = d
255: 	}
